c.tagline: The restless City of Gold, born from the world's richest goldfields.

taxi.fareNote: Metered taxis exist but most visitors use Uber or Bolt; for unmetered cabs agree the fare before setting off. Cheap minibus taxis are cash-only and used mainly by locals.

emergency.note: 112 from a mobile connects to all emergency services.

english.label: Easy to get by in English

avoid.reason: Avoid the inner-city CBD — Hillbrow, Berea and Yeoville — and township edges. High violent crime.
Carjacking and smash-and-grab at junctions — drive with doors locked; base yourself in Sandton.

hood_desc: Africa's wealthiest square mile and Johannesburg's glossy business hub, built around the Sandton City mall, Nelson Mandela Square, and a Gautrain station; leafy, secure, and full of upscale hotels and restaurants, it's where most first-timers base themselves for safety and convenience.

A polished, leafy northern suburb of malls (Rosebank Mall, The Zone), a well-known rooftop Sunday art-and-craft market, galleries, and pavement cafes, with its own Gautrain station; suits travelers who want walkable shopping, dining, and art in a secure setting.

A regenerated inner-city creative precinct on the eastern edge of downtown, known for Arts on Main, street art, design studios, weekend markets, and hip eateries; appeals to younger, culture-seeking travelers, though it's best explored by day with normal city-centre caution.

A bohemian, tree-lined residential suburb near the University of the Witwatersrand, whose 7th Street strip packs indie bars, restaurants, bookshops, and live music; a laid-back, sociable base for those who want nightlife and local character over polish.

A youthful, arts-driven student district beside Wits University, home to the Neighbourgoods Market, theatres, galleries, rooftop bars, and design shops; energetic and walkable by day, it draws a creative, going-out crowd.

water.note: Johannesburg tap water is treated and safe to drink, though supply interruptions occur.

transit.hours: The Gautrain runs roughly 5:30am-8:30pm daily (about every 12-20 min at peak); Rea Vaya, Metrobus, and Metrorail run from early morning to mid-evening with little or no late-night service.
transit.note: Most visitors rely on the Gautrain (the airport-Sandton-Pretoria spine), Uber/Bolt, or the Rea Vaya BRT; the informal minibus taxis are cheap and used widely by locals but hard for newcomers to navigate, and Metrorail commuter trains are generally best avoided.
transit.pay: The Gautrain uses a reloadable Gautrain Card (buy for ~R38/$2.30 at stations; contactless bank cards also accepted) tapped at the gates, with distance-based fares of roughly R30-206 (~$1.80-12.50). Rea Vaya BRT uses its own reloadable smartcard (~R40/$2.40). Metrobus and minibus taxis take cash.

bus: Park Station (Intercape, Greyhound, City to City)

tip.r: 10-15% at restaurants; small tips for car guards, petrol attendants, and porters are customary.

food.name: Bunny chow
food.desc: A hollowed-out half loaf of white bread filled with curry - mutton, chicken or beans - eaten with your hands using the torn-off bread lid.

places.name: Bismillah Restaurant
places.note: Long-standing Fordsburg curry house at the heart of the Indian food strip.

places.name: Akhalwaya's
places.note: Family takeaway famous for spicy mutton curry and generous bunny portions.

places.name: Oriental Plaza
places.note: Food court and shops with several counters doing quarter and half bunnies.

food.name: Kota (spatlo)
food.desc: Township street food: a quarter loaf of bread packed with chips, polony, cheese, atchar, russian sausage and a fried egg, drenched in sauce.

places.name: Vilakazi Street stalls
places.note: Vendors along Soweto's tourist strip build kotas to order all day.

places.name: Chaf Pozi
places.note: Under the Orlando cooling towers; kotas, braai and live music.

places.name: Market on Main
places.note: Sunday market where local traders sell modern takes on the kota.

food.name: Braai and boerewors
food.desc: South Africa's open-fire barbecue. Coiled boerewors sausage, lamb chops and steak grilled over wood, usually with pap and a cold beer.

places.name: Chaf Pozi
places.note: Shisa nyama under the painted Orlando Towers; pick your meat, they grill it.

places.name: Sakhumzi Restaurant
places.note: Vilakazi Street buffet of braai meats, pap, chakalaka and morogo.

places.name: The Grillhouse
places.note: Polished Joburg steakhouse for dry-aged cuts if you want it table-service.

food.name: Biltong and droewors
food.desc: Air-dried, coriander-spiced beef or game, sliced thick or shaved. Droewors is the dried sausage version; both are the national snack.

places.name: Neighbourgoods Market
places.note: Saturday market with several butchers slicing biltong to order.

places.name: Fourways Farmers Market
places.note: Weekend market with game biltong, droewors and craft producers.

places.name: Rosebank Sunday Market
places.note: Rooftop market where biltong stalls sit alongside crafts and street food.

food.name: Pap, chakalaka and morogo
food.desc: The everyday South African plate: stiff maize porridge with spicy vegetable relish, wild greens and a stew or grilled meat alongside.

places.name: Wandie's Place
places.note: Soweto institution since 1981 serving a legendary township buffet.

places.name: Moyo
places.note: Pan-African dining with face painting, marimba and a big local buffet.

places.name: Kwa Mai-Mai Market
places.note: Traditional market with cook stalls doing pap, tripe and grilled meat.

food.name: Peri-peri chicken
food.desc: Joburg's Portuguese-Mozambican heritage means flame-grilled chicken basted in fiery peri-peri, served with chips and garlic bread.

places.name: Nando's original store
places.note: The suburb where the global chain began in 1987; still a local favourite.

places.name: Parreirinha
places.note: Old-school Portuguese restaurant for prawns, chicken and trinchado.

food.name: Dom Pedro with Amarula
food.desc: South Africa's grown-up milkshake: vanilla ice cream blended with a shot of Amarula cream liqueur, ordered as dessert at almost any restaurant.

places.name: The Grillhouse
places.note: Classic steakhouse finish; ask for it after the fillet.

places.name: Moyo
places.note: Pan-African restaurant that pours generous dessert cocktails.

places.name: Sakhumzi Restaurant
places.note: Rounds off the Vilakazi Street buffet with a Dom Pedro on the terrace.

food.name: South African craft beer
food.desc: Joburg's brewing scene runs from township-born lagers to inner-city brewpubs pouring pale ales, weiss beers and stouts made on site.

places.name: Mad Giant
places.note: Brewery and taproom in the 1 Fox precinct with a striking timber interior.

places.name: Chaf Pozi
places.note: Pours Soweto Gold, the township-founded lager, alongside the braai.

places.name: Neighbourgoods Market
places.note: Rooftop bar with rotating local brewers every Saturday.

landmarks: Nelson Mandela Bridge
The elegant cable-stayed bridge linking Braamfontein to Newtown is Johannesburg's modern architectural icon, especially striking when lit at night.
Constitution Hill
A former prison and fort turned human-rights precinct, home to South Africa's Constitutional Court and an eternal flame honoring the struggle for democracy.
Apartheid Museum
A powerful, immersive museum documenting South Africa's apartheid era through its stark segregated entrances and moving exhibits — essential and unforgettable.
Gold Reef City
A theme park built atop a historic gold mine, complete with mine shaft tours and Victorian-style architecture evoking Johannesburg's gold rush origins.
Orlando Towers, Soweto
Two decommissioned cooling towers turned giant murals and bungee-jump platform are among the most photographed pieces of pop-art architecture in Africa.
Nelson Mandela Square, Sandton
A lively upscale plaza anchored by a six-meter bronze statue of Nelson Mandela, a favorite photo stop in the city's financial hub.
Mandela House, Soweto
The modest brick home where Nelson and Winnie Mandela once lived on Vilakazi Street is now a moving museum on one of the world's most historic streets.
Hector Pieterson Memorial
A somber, evocative memorial in Soweto marking the 1976 student uprising, anchored by the iconic photograph that became a symbol of resistance.
Carlton Centre (Top of Africa)
Africa's tallest office building offers the best 360-degree observation deck views over the sprawling Johannesburg skyline.
Johannesburg Skyline
The dramatic high-rise skyline, dotted with mine dumps and jacaranda-lined suburbs, is best photographed at dusk from a rooftop vantage point.

train.note: There are no scheduled international passenger trains - the cross-border services to Zimbabwe and Mozambique have been suspended for years, and the luxury Rovos Rail (https://rovos.com/) and Blue Train (https://www.bluetrain.co.za/) journeys to Victoria Falls and Dar es Salaam are holiday products, not transport. Shosholoza Meyl runs slow long-distance trains from Johannesburg Park Station to Cape Town, Durban and Musina. The Gautrain links Park Station with Sandton, Pretoria and OR Tambo airport in under an hour.

intl.op: Greyhound South Africa successors / City to City — tickets at Park Station

bus.note: Johannesburg is southern Africa's coach hub and Park Station is where almost everything starts. Intercape runs the biggest cross-border network - Maputo about 8 hours, Harare 16, Windhoek 20 - and buses are far more practical than trains for these routes. Carry your passport and expect long waits at Beitbridge and Lebombo. Book online well ahead; Park Station itself needs normal city caution.

ferry.note: Johannesburg is 1,750 m up on the Highveld, hundreds of kilometres from the sea, so there are no ferries.

half.name: Cradle of Humankind & Sterkfontein Caves
half.blurb: A UNESCO fossil site with limestone caves that have yielded some of the world's oldest hominid remains, about an hour from Johannesburg.

half.name: Hartbeespoort Dam
half.blurb: A reservoir in the Magaliesberg mountains with a cableway, boat rides, and lakeside restaurants, about an hour from Johannesburg.

half.name: Cullinan
half.blurb: A historic mining town where the largest diamond ever found was unearthed, with underground mine tours, about an hour from Johannesburg.

full.name: Pilanesberg National Park
full.blurb: A Big Five game reserve set inside an extinct volcanic crater, roughly two and a half hours from Johannesburg.
